page: Microsoft Azure E192ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by Microsoft Hyper-V and based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The instance supplies 192 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 480 MB of L3 cache and hardware extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. The system couples this compute foundation with 1536 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, and integrates 11340 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The configuration includes zero discrete GPUs.

Benchmark assessments confirm top-tier performance in parallel computation, memory throughput, and storage-intensive database tasks. The instance logged a multi-core stress-ng metric of 202544.14 and a PassMark CPU score of 152200.24, both falling in the top ten percent of tested hardware. Memory throughput is similarly robust, demonstrating 687.65 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 270.43 GB/sec on writes. In synthetic and application-specific tests, the server executed 252.84 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved top-tier marks in PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-thread stress-ng scores align with the middle 50 percent, indicating that processing density relies on aggregate parallel scaling rather than individual core velocity.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, bundling over 11 TB of high-throughput NVMe SSD storage with high-density system memory minimizes the overhead of provisioning external networked block storage for heavy I/O operations. The hardware layout is best matched to enterprise-scale in-memory databases such as Redis or SAP HANA, high-concurrency transactional database engines, distributed analytical processing, and extract-transform-load workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E192ds_v7 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 192 vCPUs across 96 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores running at 4.2 GHz, 1536 GB of RAM, and 11340 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V without discrete GPUs, it achieves an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio alongside 480 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions. Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded execution with a stress-ng score of 202544.14 and memory read bandwidth exceeding 687 GB/sec. Application testing showcases high enterprise throughput, yielding 252.84 million Redis SET operations per second and leading database benchmark marks. While single-threaded processing performs at median levels, the dense core count, massive memory capacity, and substantial bundled NVMe storage make this instance well suited for large in-memory caching systems, distributed transactional databases, enterprise data warehousing, and demanding parallel data processing pipelines.
